chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليهما السلام, from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام.
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“And let not pity for them seize you in the religion of Allah.”
He said: “In carrying out the prescribed punishments.” And regarding His saying, Exalted is He:
“And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.”
He said: “The group is one person.” And he said: “The person liable to a prescribed punishment is not made to swear an oath.”

key_terms.إِقَامَةِ الْحُدُودِ: the enforcement and execution of the prescribed legal punishments
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the believers who witness the punishment
key_terms.دِينِ اللَّهِ: the religion and legal order ordained by Allah in this context
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْحَدِّ: the person upon whom a prescribed punishment is due
key_terms.طَائِفَةٌ: a group; here interpreted as even one person
key_terms.عَذَابَهُمَا: their punishment, referring to the penal consequence being witnessed
key_terms.يُسْتَحْلَفُ: is required to swear an oath

ai.seo_question: How is the verse about not showing pity in the religion of Allah explained in relation to hudud?
ai.summary: This report explains two Qur'anic phrases related to the implementation of hudud. It interprets “in the religion of Allah” as referring to the enforcement of prescribed punishments, and clarifies that the witnessing group may consist of even one believer; it also states that a person subject to hadd is not put under oath.
